1.title: Network Service Issues
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty-two: Network Service Issues. It covers the exam area five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. five point three Given a scenario, troubleshoot common issues with network services: switching issues (S T P: network loops, root bridge selection, port roles, port states. Incorrect V L A N assignment. A C Ls). Route selection (routing table, default routes). Address pool exhaustion. Incorrect default gateway. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five point zero Network Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Switching issues
1.text: Switching issues. S T P network loop. Broadcast storm, very high C P U, M A C table flapping, network crawls; check S T P, find the missing or misconfigured blocking port or an unmanaged switch loop. Wrong root bridge. A small access switch becomes root, so traffic takes inefficient paths; set the intended core switch with the lowest priority. Port roles and states. Check which ports are root, designated, blocked; a port stuck in blocking or listening during convergence explains no traffic.

1.title: Switching issues, continued
1.text: Switching issues. Incorrect V L A N assignment. A host in the wrong V L A N cannot reach its gateway or peers; check the access port's V L A N. A C L blocking. Traffic denied by a rule or the implicit deny; review A C L order and direction.

1.title: Switching issues, continued
1.text: Switching issues. The figure shows this: Quick triage: no link, wrong I P, no gateway, no D N S, blocked by A C L.

1.title: Routing issues
1.text: Routing issues. Routing table. Check whether a route to the destination exists ( show route ) and which is selected. Default route missing or wrong. Traffic to unknown networks (the internet) has nowhere to go. Route selection. A more specific or lower-A D route may be sending traffic the wrong way.

1.title: Addressing issues
1.text: Addressing issues. Address pool exhaustion. New clients get no address (or A P I P A one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four dot x dot x); scope full: shorten lease time, enlarge the scope, remove stale leases. Incorrect default gateway. Local access works, nothing off the subnet works. Incorrect I P address. Wrong subnet, so the host cannot reach its gateway. Duplicate I P address. Intermittent connectivity for two hosts, "address conflict" warnings; find the duplicate with A R P, use D H C P reservations. Incorrect subnet mask. Host cannot reach some local addresses, or thinks remote hosts are local. Exam tip: Can reach local hosts but not the internet: check the default gateway. Intermittent connection for two hosts: duplicate I P address. one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four dot x dot x: no D H C P or pool exhausted.

1.title: A fast triage
1.text: A fast triage. Ping one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot zero dot one. T C P or I P stack on the host. Ping own I P. N I C or address configuration. Ping the default gateway. Local link, V L A N, mask, gateway address. Ping a remote I P. Routing, A C L, nat. Ping a name. D N S. Exam tip: Local works but remote fails: gateway. one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four dot x dot x: D H C P. Intermittent for two hosts: duplicate I P. Storm and M A C flapping: loop. Exam tip: Test from the bottom up: link, address and gateway, then routing, then D N S. The first failing step names the layer.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A network slows to a crawl, switch C P Us spike, and M A C addresses flap between ports. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A switching loop with spanning tree not blocking redundant paths. Loops cause broadcast storms and M A C table flapping.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. New laptops receive one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four dot x dot x addresses while older devices work. What is the most likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The D H C P scope is exhausted. A full scope leaves new clients without leases.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A host can reach other devices on its subnet but nothing beyond. What should be checked first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The default gateway setting. An incorrect default gateway blocks off-subnet traffic.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Two workstations lose connectivity intermittently and each shows an I P address conflict message. What is the cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A duplicate I P address. Duplicate I P s cause conflicts and intermittent access.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. After a switch replacement a user in the Finance V L A N cannot reach the Finance gateway. The port is up. What should be checked? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The access port's V L A N assignment. A wrong V L A N on the access port isolates the host.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Internet traffic fails while internal traffic works, and the router has no route for zero dot zero dot zero dot zero slash zero. What should be added? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A default route. Without a default route, unknown destinations are unreachable.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four dot x dot x indicate? Answer: The host could not get a D H C P address (A P I P A). Question two. What symptom does a duplicate I P address cause? Answer: Intermittent connectivity and address conflict messages. Question three. What happens when an incorrect default gateway is set? Answer: Local traffic works but off-subnet traffic fails.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does S T P prevent? Answer: Layer two loops. Question five. What command shows the routing table? Answer: show route (ip route or route print on hosts). Question six. What does pinging the gateway test? Answer: The local link, V L A N, mask and gateway configuration.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Switching: S T P loops (storm, M A C flap), wrong root, V L A N assignment, A C L implicit deny. Routing: routing table, default route, route selection. Addressing: pool exhaustion (A P I P A), gateway, I P, duplicate I P, subnet mask. Triage: loopback, own I P, gateway, remote I P, name.
